# SHAPI

> SHAPI finds the code that breaks when a third-party API changes (a renamed field, a new status code, a retired version or model), and fixes it test-first: it writes a contract test that fails before the fix and passes after, and opens a pull request.

Advisories are open data (CC BY 4.0). Each lists the endpoint, what changed, the effective date, and what to do.

## Docs

- [FAQ](https://shapi.dev/faq): Common questions about SHAPI: languages, providers, pull request limits, AI and licensing.
- [Coding agents (MCP)](https://shapi.dev/guide/agents): Use SHAPI from Claude Code, Cursor and other coding agents, through the CLI or the MCP server.
- [CLI reference](https://shapi.dev/guide/cli): Every shapi-cli command, option, exit code and environment variable.
- [Fix tiers](https://shapi.dev/guide/fix-tiers): How far SHAPI trusts its fixes for each recipe, provider and kind of change, and the benchmark runs that earned it.
- [How fixes are verified](https://shapi.dev/guide/fixes): How SHAPI proves a fix: a contract test that fails before the change and passes after it, run in a sandbox.
- [GitHub App](https://shapi.dev/guide/github-app): What the SHAPI GitHub App does on each push, the permissions it asks for, its pull request limits, and plans.
- [How SHAPI works](https://shapi.dev/guide/how-it-works): How SHAPI maps your third-party API calls into an api.lock, matches them against advisories, and fixes what breaks.
- [Quickstart](https://shapi.dev/guide/quickstart): Scan a repository for the code a third-party API change breaks, then fix it test-first. Two commands, no account.
- [Spec churn index](https://shapi.dev/guide/spec-churn): How often each API provider's OpenAPI spec changes in a way that breaks clients, measured over the full history of the APIs.guru directory.
- [Security and code handling](https://shapi.dev/security): What SHAPI reads, runs and stores when it scans and fixes your code, and how customers are kept apart.
